answer: Every finished job is hashed onto the wharf board, with a 60-credit bond locked per identity. Once each tide, auditors sweep the board for duplicate hashes: a second filing of the same work burns both bonds, since the registry punishes the pair rather than guessing the original. A rented relic, an old output resold to a new identity, triggers the same double burn, so a rental ring loses twice per reuse. The kth fake identity needs a kth new job plus its own 60 credits; 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits and 1,000 distinct jobs. An honest agent files one original job and keeps its bond.
